name: Programs
description: Milestones, dependencies, risks and decisions across all programs. One integrated timeline per program by function with baselines, slips with reasons, the critical path, stage gates, a RAID log, monthly updates and frozen leadership reports; cash at key milestones when Runway is used.
whenToUse: A small biotech (roughly 10–50 people) needs one integrated view of program milestones, dependencies, gates, risks and monthly status without enterprise PPM: an integrated timeline per program across CMC, nonclinical, clinical and regulatory, the critical path, slips with reasons, gate readiness and a monthly leadership report.
whenNotToUse: Task-level project management (use the team's task tool), resource and capacity planning, portfolio prioritisation or rNPV, budgets (use Runway), timesheets, Kanban boards, document approval workflows, validated GxP or Part 11 project records, and any patient-level data.

heading.description: App heading shown above every screen.

tableMap.description: JSON object keyed by stable role key: core data contract v1 roles programs (required) and people (optional, read only here); app roles programs.plan_items, programs.slips, programs.decisions, programs.raid, programs.updates, programs.reports, programs.settings; optional read-only runway.month_closes (Runway snapshots). Each value is {typeId:<authorized table UUID>, fields:{<logical key>:<real field key>}, writableFields:[<logical keys>]}. Real keys are lowercase snake_case.

pageSize.description: Rows per page in registers, 10–50; the template clamps the value.

layoutProfile.description: JSON presentation profile written only by native layout settings through a reviewed, versioned app update.

readOnly.description: When true, the app proposes no writes even for users who may edit.

demoLabel.description: Label the app as a fictional demo. Only for the repository preview.

asOfOverride.description: Optional fixed as-of date (YYYY-MM-DD) for previews and tests only. Leave empty: the app uses today's date from the app runtime.

instructions:
Programs 2.0.0 is a custom frontend-js program-management app that follows docs/product/MODULAR_APPS_AND_SHARED_DATA.md: the shared programs and people tables use the core data contract v1 role keys, app tables use programs.* role keys, features that use another app's data degrade gracefully, and removing an app or tab never deletes data. It replaces Project Oversight 1.0.1 for new installs; saved 1.0.1 apps are not migrated.

1. Discover and pin. Read read_app_template_guidance (usage, then authoring when extending) to the last nextOffset, read_app_design, list_app_templates and read_app_template for life.project-oversight. Pin this exact version and digest and keep one requestKey for the creation.
2. Install and reuse. Before installing, call list_archived_items (kind apps, this templateId); if an archived Programs app exists, offer to restore it first. The platform Use action shows the shared-data choice: when a compatible programs table already exists (for example created by Runway), reusing it is the default and no second programs table is created; the user can choose separate data instead (for a confidential program, use a separate app with separate data in a restricted project). An existing people table and Runway's month closes are connected the same way when present; they are never created by Programs. When preparing the app yourself with prepare_app_from_template, bind those existing tables under the same role keys with explicit bindings, unless the user explicitly chooses separate data. Never seed demo data.
3. Map fields. tableMap maps each stable role key to an authorized table. Core roles use exactly the core data contract v1 fields; never rename, retype or remove them. Programs owns the optional programs fields health, health_rationale and health_date. Use multiple:false, lowercase snake_case real keys and scalar record-ID text for relationships (program_id, predecessor_id, plan_item_id, linked_item_id). runway.month_closes and people are read only in Programs.
4. First plan in one session. From a development plan, slide, spreadsheet or description the user shares, propose one reviewed batch: the program record (stage required), 10–40 plan items with function, owner, dates, item_type and one predecessor each (create items before their successors, or in a second batch once the first receipt IDs exist), the first gates with criteria lines and top risks. Do not set baselines in that batch. When the user confirms the plan, they set the baseline in Plan (Set baseline), or you propose baseline_start/baseline_end equal to the current dates for review.
5. Dates move. A later end_date on a planned, in-progress or at-risk item that has a baseline needs a reason; the reviewed save writes the item and exactly one programs.slips record {plan_item_id, changed_on, old_end, new_end, days, reason, detail}. Show the downstream preview (successors start the day after their predecessor's new end) and move successors only if the user accepts them in the same review. Reject a predecessor that would create a cycle.
6. Gates. Criteria are lines starting with [met], [not met] or [open]. Prepare the gate pack (criteria status, open risks, recent decisions) on request. Never set a gate outcome or a program's health yourself: the user records them; follow-up milestones are created or cancelled in the same review as the outcome.
7. Monthly updates and leadership report. Draft programs.updates text from recorded changes (slips, decisions, closed and new risks) without inventing progress; the user reviews it. The app assembles and freezes the month's report; saved reports never change.
8. Customization: layout changes use the native gear (tracker:layout → prepare_tool_layout); business settings use a reviewed write to the programs.settings row; extra fields need a reviewed schema change and a separately reviewed app revision. Revise the same saved app; preserve IDs, bindings and access.
9. Automations are optional and configured only after the app is saved: a monthly update reminder email, a slip notice email for key milestones and a monthly status draft on the Claude or ChatGPT runner. The app never waits for them.

quickStart: Read the current usage/authoring guidance and this template's documentation; pin life.project-oversight 2.0.0 and its digest with one requestKey.

Before installing, check for an archived Programs app and offer to restore it. Use installs it; keep the default to reuse an existing programs table (e.g. from Runway) unless the user wants separate data.
Settings → Add program: name, stage and lead. Optionally edit settings (function lanes, stages, health definitions, due-soon window, update day).

Plan → Add item for milestones and key activities with function, owner, dates, status and one predecessor; mark the decisive milestones as key. Or ask the assistant to build a first plan from a document you share.
Plan → Set baseline when the plan is agreed. Timeline then shows baseline ghost bars, the critical path and slips.
Gates & decisions → Add gate with criteria; RAID → add top risks; Updates → monthly update per program, then save the month's leadership report.
documentation.dataContract: Stable role keys. Core data contract v1: programs (name text*, code text, indication text, modality select small_molecule/biologic/antibody/cell_therapy/gene_therapy/rna/vaccine/device/other, stage select* discovery/preclinical/ind_enabling/phase_1/phase_2/phase_3/registration/approved, lead text, status select active/paused/stopped/partnered, archived boolean; Programs-owned optional fields health select unassessed/green/amber/red, health_rationale text, health_date date) and people (name*, organization_id, title, email, archived; optional, read only in Programs; owner fields stay plain text names). App tables: programs.plan_items (name text*, program_id text* record ID of programs, item_type select* milestone/activity, function select* cmc/nonclinical/clinical/regulatory/other, owner text, start_date date, end_date date* (the milestone date for milestones), baseline_start date, baseline_end date, status select* planned/in_progress/done/at_risk/cancelled, predecessor_id text record ID of one plan_items record (finish-to-start, no lag), is_key boolean, notes text, archived boolean); programs.slips (plan_item_id text*, changed_on date*, old_end date*, new_end date*, days number*, reason select* scientific/cro_vendor/regulatory/manufacturing/funding/other, detail text); programs.decisions (name text*, program_id text*, kind select* gate/decision, target_date date, criteria text one per line [met]/[not met]/[open], outcome select pending/go/no_go/conditional/decided, decided_on date, approver text, options text, rationale text, linked_item_id text record ID of a plan item or RAID entry, archived boolean); programs.raid (name text*, program_id text, raid_type select* risk/assumption/issue/dependency, likelihood and impact select low/medium/high, owner text, mitigation text, next_review date, status select* open/monitoring/closed, linked_item_id text, archived boolean); programs.updates (program_id text*, month date* first day, health select*, rationale, summary, next_steps, author text); programs.reports (month date*, title text*, narrative text, contents text frozen JSON written once by the app, saved_on date); programs.settings (one row: functions and stages comma lists of enabled options in display order, health_definitions text, due_soon_days number default 90, update_day number default 5). Partner output, read only: runway.month_closes (month, closed, currency, metrics frozen JSON v2) from Runway. App output for other apps: programs.plan_items with is_key (Runway reads key milestones) and programs.reports. Every field is scalar multiple:false; relationships are record IDs, never names. Slip rule: a later end_date on a planned, in_progress or at_risk item with a baseline creates exactly one slips record in the same review. Health is always a human judgement with a date and rationale; the app never sets it. Access is app-level only: no per-screen protection is advertised. Hiding a program is not security; use a separate app with separate data in a restricted project. Reads are bounded to 800 rows per table; partial reads disable the critical path and totals.
documentation.interactionContract: Seven screens with stable IDs for the native layout gear: overview, timeline, plan, decisions, raid, updates, settings; column groups items, raid and decisions. Overview: next key milestone (with Runway cash when connected), KPIs (overdue items, slips this quarter with total days, on-time rate of baselined milestones done this quarter), program cards (stage, health with assessment date and a flag when older than 45 days or unassessed, next milestone and days to it, open high risks), next N days (items, gates and decisions; N = due_soon_days), slips this quarter with top reasons, exceptions (missing monthly update, overdue milestones, gates without criteria, risks past review, stale health, predecessor cycles and overlaps). Timeline: Gantt by program and function lane, milestones as diamonds, baseline ghost bars, today line, critical path highlighted; click a bar for "what drives this date" (its predecessor chain) and Edit dates; bars never move by drag; program and function filters; 60 items per page; a table fallback; Present mode (read-only one-page timeline with key milestones, original vs current dates and slip reasons); cash and cushion markers at key milestones from the latest Runway snapshot (green ≥ 6 months, amber 3–6, red < 3) when runway.month_closes is connected and readable, otherwise hidden with a one-line note. Plan: register with search, filters (program, function, status, owner, date window), 25 rows per page, Details with slip story, Add/Edit/Duplicate/Archive, Set baseline per program and Reset baseline (reason kept in notes). The item editor shows the slip reason when required and the downstream preview with an accept checkbox. Gates & decisions: upcoming gates with criteria checklist, readiness and days to the gate; Record outcome (go/no-go/conditional/decided, date, approver, rationale, follow-up milestones to create, planned milestones to cancel, all in one review); decisions log linked to items or risks. RAID: 3 × 3 likelihood × impact matrix (click to filter), register, promote assumption → risk or risk → issue (new linked entry, original closed). Updates: monthly updates, leadership report assembly with preview, frozen save, archive with read-only view and Markdown export text. Settings: business settings row, programs with health assessment, links to platform Access and Automations. Every input carries data-ui-state and a stable data-action; failed saves keep the draft.
documentation.lifecycle: A fresh preview renders with no writes. After the app is saved, every create, edit, archive, baseline, slip, gate outcome, promotion and report save is an exact records.propose batch (≤ 50 writes) that the user approves in the host review; the app shows a notice until then and the database is unchanged. Edits capture the record version when the editor opens; successors moved by an accepted downstream preview and milestones cancelled by a gate outcome carry the versions captured when the editor or gate opened, so a concurrent edit is rejected, not overwritten. Reconcile ambiguous saves by receipt; never retry with a new key. Saved reports are frozen; their contents never change after later edits. The as-of date is today's date from the app runtime and only filters the view (due soon, overdue, quarter); slips record changed_on and reports saved_on as that date. Layout changes are presentation-only reviewed app updates; saved configuration is re-read on every render. Archiving or deleting the app archives it and keeps all tables and records; restoring brings its automations back switched off. Removing a tab unbinds it; adding it back reconnects the same tables. Installing again first offers to restore an archived Programs app.
limitations: One predecessor per item, finish-to-start, no lags or other dependency types; no resources, capacity or percent-complete roll-ups.
App-level access only: per-screen restrictions are not advertised for this custom app. Confidential programs need a separate app with separate data in a restricted project.
Reads are bounded to 800 rows per table; larger plans show partial data and withhold the critical path and totals.
Present mode cannot export an image file inside custom apps; use a screenshot or print to PDF. Report export is copyable Markdown text.
Cash markers need Runway 2.1 snapshots connected as runway.month_closes and readable by the viewer; reserve-based cushions from Runway settings are not used (cushion is to cash-out).
Automations are optional; the status-draft research needs a connected Claude or ChatGPT runner. No GxP or Part 11 claims.

examples.prompt: Set up Programs for PX-101 from this development plan (fictional): IND-enabling small molecule, GMP batch to January, tox to February, IND end of March, first participant dosed end of May.
examples.expectedBehavior: Pins the template, installs or prepares the app (reusing an existing programs table), proposes one reviewed batch with the program and plan items by function with predecessors, then the gate and top risks; sets no baseline until the user confirms the plan.

examples.prompt: The GMP batch moves from 31 January to 21 February because of the CDMO. What happens to the IND date?
examples.expectedBehavior: Explains the critical path and the downstream preview (drug product release, IND package, IND submission shift by 21 days); prepares the item edit with reason cro_vendor and exactly one slip; moves successors only if the user accepts them in the same review.

examples.prompt: Prepare the gate pack for the IND go / no-go.
examples.expectedBehavior: Reads the gate criteria (met / not met / open), open risks and recent decisions; summarises readiness and days to the gate; does not record an outcome.

examples.prompt: Draft the October updates for both programs and the leadership report.
examples.expectedBehavior: Drafts programs.updates text from recorded slips, decisions and risk changes without inventing progress and proposes them for review; the user saves the frozen report in Updates.

examples.prompt: We do not want any automations.
examples.expectedBehavior: Leaves the app fully usable with none; updates, slips and reports work manually.

tasks.whenUseful: Three optional automations; no automation is a fully supported path. (1) Monthly update reminder: a TrialAgents email action on a monthly calendar on update_day, Europe/Berlin, to program leads who are registered members with app access, listing programs without an update for the month. (2) Slip notice: a TrialAgents email action triggered by creation of a programs.slips record for an item with is_key = true, to the owner, stating the item, old and new date, days and reason. (3) Monthly status draft: research on the shared Claude or ChatGPT runner after the update day; reads last month's slips, decisions and closed or new risks and proposes draft programs.updates text for human review, writing only to programs.updates under a narrow expiring grant. Manual path: the team writes updates in the app and checks Overview exceptions; nothing waits for automation.
tasks.readRequirements: Reminder: programs (name, lead, status), programs.updates (program_id, month), programs.settings.update_day. Slip notice: programs.slips (plan_item_id, old_end, new_end, days, reason, detail) and programs.plan_items (name, owner, is_key). Status draft: programs.slips, programs.decisions, programs.raid and existing programs.updates for the month (deduplication).
tasks.outputContract: Reminder: one email per recipient per month listing programs without an update; no_update when every active program has one. Slip notice: one email per created slip on a key milestone; never for non-key items. Status draft: at most one programs.updates record per program and month (dedup key program_id + month); never overwrites an existing update; never sets program health in the programs table; partial source reads are reported and nothing is written for incomplete programs.
tasks.promptExample: Monthly, the day after the update day (Europe/Berlin): for each active program in Programs, read last month's slips, gate and decision outcomes, and RAID entries opened or closed. If the program has no programs.updates record for last month, propose one draft update {program_id, month: first day of last month, health: unassessed unless the user's latest assessment applies, rationale, summary, next_steps, author: "Draft by assistant"} built only from those records, citing them. Do not invent progress or change any other table. If every program already has an update, report no_update.
